outcomes.name: each trial's own registered primary outcome

primary.poolable_reason: WARFARIN IS THE COMPARATOR IN BOTH TRIALS, AND THE OUTCOMES DIFFER AS WELL. NCT00262600 is RE-LY, which tests DABIGATRAN against warfarin in atrial fibrillation with a registered primary of 'Yearly Event Rate for Composite Endpoint of Stroke/SEE'. NCT02942407 tests APIXABAN against warfarin in haemodialysis patients with atrial fibrillation, with a registered primary of ISTH-defined BLEEDING. So the page's own titled drug is the control in both, the two experimental drugs are different, and one primary is an efficacy composite while the other is a safety endpoint. THE OLMESARTAN SHAPE, confirmed by reading rather than by a gate verdict -- and note that RE-LY types every arm ACTIVE_COMPARATOR, so an arm-type check alone would have called warfarin a comparator here for the wrong reason.

primary.what_this_verdict_does_not_establish: NOT that any of these trials is poor -- each is registered, randomised where it says so, and reports its primary. NOT that the drug is ineffective. NOT that no poolable question exists in this area: only that the question this page's title asks cannot be answered by pooling the trials this page carries. If a further eligible trial is identified, this verdict should be revisited.

risk_of_bias_verdict: Not assessed. A risk-of-bias assessment grades trials contributing to a pooled result, and this page publishes none.
